The 4670-gram (10-pound 5-ounce) male neonate Terme delivered after prolonged labor to a 26-year-old female. The Apgar score is 9 and 9 at both 1 and 5 minutes. Delivery room tests show swelling, sensitivity, and cryptis above the left clavicle. The left upper limb has slowed down. Movement of the hands and wrists is normal. Grass reflex is normal in both hands. An asymmetric Moro reflex is present. The rest of the test shows no abnormalities, and an anteroposterior X-ray confirms the diagnosis. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
A. Nerve conductivity test
B. Surgical fixation
C. Physical therapy
D. Pin Sleeve on Shirt
E. arm splinting
F. MRI of the clavicle

A 66-year-old male brought a 3-month history of fatigue to the doctor. He has high blood pressure and hyperlipidemia. He suffered a transient ischemic attack 3 years ago. He drinks 3 beers a day, and sometimes 2 more at social events. He is currently receiving aspirin, simvastatin, hydrochlorothiazide, and metoprolol. Its temperature is 37.1 ° C (98.8 ° F), pulse is 78, respiration is 19 per minute, and oxygen saturation in room air is 97%. He is in no discomfort but looks distinctly pale and has a series of needle-like small, red, non-blanching spots on his limbs. His spleen is remarkably large to the touch. Laboratory results show hemoglobin at 8.0 grams per deciliter, leukocyte count at 80,000 / cubic মি.লি., and platelet count at 34,000 / cubic মি.লি. A blood smear shows immature cells with large, clear nucleoli and pink, elongated, needle-shaped cytoplasmic inclusions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Cirrhosis
B. Acute lymphoblastic leukemia
C. Chronic myelogenous leukemia
D. Myelodysplastic syndrome
E. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia
F. Acute myelogenous leukemia

A 40-year-old male approached the patient as he has been experiencing watery diarrhea and periodic abdominal crampy pain for the past 5-months. She has no fever, nausea, or vomiting. In the last 6 months, he has lost 1.8-কেজি (4-lb) weight, although there is no loss of appetite. His wife has noticed that sometimes his face and throat turn red after meals or during times of stress. He had been diagnosed with asthma a year earlier. He is suffering from high blood pressure. Current medications include albuterol inhalers and enalapril. He drinks a beer every day. He has a temperature of 36.7 ° C (98 ° F), a pulse of 85 / min, and a blood pressure 130/85 mmHg of mercury. The respiratory system sounds clear. The grade 2 / 6 systolic murmur is best heard in the left sternal border and fourth intercostal space. The abdomen is soft, there is light palpation, no guarding or rebound. The rest of the body exam shows no abnormalities. The complete blood count is within the reference range. If left untreated, this patient will be at the highest risk of any of the following conditions?
A. Asphyxia
B. Achlorhydria
C. T-cell lymphoma
D. Megaloblastic anemia
E. Dementia
F. Intestinal fistula
G. Arthritis

A 4-year-old boy has been brought to the emergency department because of severe abdominal pain and bilious vomiting that has been occurring for 6 hours. He has not had any bowel movements in the last 24 hours. He looks sick. It has a temperature of 37.8 ° C (100 ° F) and a pulse of 122 beats per minute. On examination, a swollen abdomen is seen. There is sensitivity to touch in the lower abdomen; protective contractions and reflex sensitivity are present. The sound of the bowels has decreased. An abdominal X-ray shows a distended bowel. He has a 14-year-old brother with him. The surgeon recommended an emergency laparotomy. The parents have gone to a friend's house and are not reachable. Which of the following would be the best next step for management?
A. Get consent from the patient's brother
B. Obtain consent from the patient.
C. Get a court order for surgery.
D. Set the hospital's ethical advice.
E. Perform an emergency laparotomy
F. Delay surgery until parental consent is obtained.

A 9-year-old girl was brought to the emergency department with a headache and double vision, an hour after being hit in the head while she was playing with a friend. His friend's elbow struck his head, just above the left ear. She did not lose consciousness, but her mother reported that she was disoriented for 20 minutes after the incident and could not recall the injury. She looks healthy. He is alert and aware of persons, places, and times. Its temperature is 37.2 ° C (99 ° F), pulse is 86 / min, respiration is 15 / min, and blood pressure is 118/78 mmHg. On examination, the head is tilted towards the right shoulder. A photo of the eye is shown in the initial view. There is slight sensitivity to touch in the left temporal bone. Impairment of vision in both eyes when examined individually 20/20. Hypertropia of the patient's left eye increases when looking to the right and when the patient tilts their head to the left shoulder. The pupillae are equal and reactive to light. Muscle strength and sensation are intact on both sides. Deep tendon reflex 2 + on both sides. The plantar reflex responds to flexure. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's eye symptoms?
A. Oculomotor nerve damage
B. Retrobalbar hemorrhage
C. Trochlear nerve damage
D. Medial longitudinal fasciculus damage
E. Dorsal midbrain damage
F. abducens nerve damage

A mother takes her 3-year-old son to the pediatrician because he is doing tantrums. The boy has no history of serious disease and is on track for developmental milestones. Her mother recently went back to work 2 weeks ago. She explains that since then, her son does a tantrum almost every other morning, usually when she dresses him up or drops him off at daycare. She cries loudly for about 5 minutes, says she doesn't want to go to the daycare and moves her arms and legs. According to the daycare staff, she behaves well throughout the day. In the evenings, he does tantrums twice a week, usually when he is told he has to finish his meals or it is time to go to bed. These tantrums have been happening for about 6 months. The mother is concerned that her son may have a behavioral disorder. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the boy's behavior?
A. Autism spectrum disorder
B. Conduct disorder
C. Normal development
D. Oppositional Defiant Disorder
E. Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
F. Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder

A 45-year-old male patient came to the doctor with severe left knee pain and swelling. He has hypercholesterolemia and high blood pressure. Current medications include pravastatin and captopril. He adopts a low-fat diet consisting of fish and leafy greens. He drinks 4 to 6 cups of coffee every day. He has smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for 26 years and drinks 2 - 3 beers a day. Life expectancy is within normal limits. Examination of the left knee shows swelling, warmth, and severe sensitivity to touch. Arthrocentesis is performed. Gram stain is negative. Monosodium urate crystals can be seen in synovial fluid analysis. Which of the following health maintenance recommendations is best suited to prevent the recurrence of symptoms?
A. turn off captopril
B. Start the aspirin.
C. replace beer with red wine
D. Quit smoking
E. Reduce your coffee intake
F. Reduce the intake of fish
G. Stop Provastatin
H. start colchicine

A previously healthy 32-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his girlfriend following a seizure. Earlier that day, he experienced a nosebleed that took 30 minutes to stop with pressure. He has no history of exposure or epilepsy or any other seizure disorder. He is not taking any medication. He has a temperature of 39.1 ° C (102.4 ° F), a pulse of 106 beats per minute, a respiratory rate of 26 beats per minute, and a blood pressure of 128/70 mmHg. He is confused and disoriented. Examination shows pale coloration and diffuse petechiae on the trunk and arms. The throat is soft, and neurological examination is within the otherwise normal range. Laboratory tests show that: Hemoglobin 9 grams per deciliter Leukocyte count 8,200 per cubic mm Platelet count 34,000 per cubic mm Prothrombin time is 13 seconds Partial thromboplastin time 30 seconds Fibrin Split Product Negative Serum: Creatinine 2.9 mg per deciliter Bilirubin total of 3.2 mg per deciliter Bilirubin directly 0. 4 milligram per deciliter Lactate dehydrogenase 559 units per liter A lateral blood smear shows a large number of schistocytes. Which of the following would be the most appropriate next step in management?
A. Electroencephalography
B. Packed red blood cell transfusion
C. CT scan of the head
D. Plasma exchange therapy
E. Fresh Frozen Plasma Transfusion
F. MRI scan of the head
G. Platelet transfusion
H. Tranexamic acid in the veins

A 67-year-old male came to the emergency department this morning to be evaluated for 2 episodes of red urine. He has no pain during urination. He reported lower back pain and fever. He was diagnosed with right knee osteoarthritis 6 months ago, which he manages with 1 - 2 tablets of ibuprofen a day. He has smoked a pack of cigarettes every day for the past 45 years. He doesn't drink alcohol. It has a temperature of 38.5 ° C (101.3 ° F), a pulse of 95 per minute, and a blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg. Physical examination reveals mild, diffuse maculopapular scarring and bilateral flank pain. No abnormalities are found in the rest of the test. Urinalysis shows: Blood + 3 Protein + 1 High-flying field per RBC 10-12 RBC Cast Negative Eosinophils are abundant Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Acute tubulointerstitial nephritis
B. Acute pyelonephritis
C. Acute glomerulonephritis
D. Crystal-induced acute kidney damage
E. Carcinoma of the kidney cells
F. Henkh-Shonline Purpura
G. Acute tubular necrosis

The 50-year-old male patient came to the doctor with a history of difficulty having sex due to 6-month erectile dysfunction. His type 2 diabetes mellitus is well controlled with metformin. He doesn't smoke. He drinks 5 to 6 beers every day. Signs of his life are within normal limits. Physical examination shows bilateral leg swelling, decreased testicular volume, and increased breast tissue. The ribs are palpable 2 cm below the left costal margin. Abdominal ultrasound shows atrophic, hyperechoic, nodular liver. Upper endoscopy shows submucosal veins 2 millimeters in diameter with red spots on the surface in the distal esophagus. He began therapy with sildenafil for erectile dysfunction. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management of oesophagus changes in this patient?
A. Injection sclerotherapy
B. Nadolol therapy
C. Losaratan therapy
D. octreotide therapy
E. Isosorbide mononitrate therapy
F. Endoscopic band ligation
G. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt
H. Metoprolol therapy

A 45-year-old woman approached the clinic because of fatigue and irregular menstrual cycles for the past year. He also complained of recurrent sinus infections. In the last 6 months, he has experienced increased urination and swelling of the legs. Additionally, he has had difficulty lifting his 3-year-old niece for the past 3 weeks. He was recently diagnosed with depression. He worked as a medical assistant. The patient has smoked a half-pack of cigarettes every day for the past 25 years and drinks four beers on weekends. His only medication is escitalopram. He is 160 cm (5 ft 3 in) tall and weighs 79 kg (175 lb); BMI is 31 kg / m2. He looks tired. Its temperature is 37 ° C (98.6 ° F), pulse 80 / min, respiration 18 / min, and blood pressure 140/82 mmHg. Physical examination reveals an obese throat and a large belly. Skin examination shows multiple bluish spots on the arms and legs. There is general weakness and atrophy of the proximal muscles. The laboratory results show: Serum Sodium 150 milliequivalent / litre Potassium 3. 0 milliequivalent / litre Chloride 103 milliequivalent / litre Bicarbonate 30 milliequivalent / litre Urea nitrogen 19 mg / deciliter Creatinine 0.9 mg / deciliter Glucose 136 mg / dl In the 1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test, serum cortisol is 167 nanomoles / liter (normal < 50) and 24-hour urinary cortisol is 425 micrograms (normal < 300 micrograms). Serum ACTH is 169 picograms / milliliter (normal = 7-50). Later, high-dose dexamethasone suppression assays showed serum cortisol levels of 164 nanomoles / liter (normal < 50). Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of the patient's symptoms?
A. Extrinsic corticosteroid intake
B. Pituitary adenoma
C. Adrenal carcinoma
D. Hypothyroidism
E. Pheochromocytoma
F. Small cell lung cancer
G. Adrenal adenoma

A 24-year-old primigravid female, at 38 weeks of gestation, visits the doctor for a gynecological visit. At the last two gynecological visits, transabdominal ultrasound showed the baby in the breech position. She has no medical issues and only takes pre-natal vitamins. His pulse is 95 / min, respiratory rate is 16 / min, and blood pressure is 130/76 mmHg. The abdomen is soft and insensitive; no contractions are felt. Pelvic examination shows closed cervical oesophagus and uterus consistent with 38 weeks gestation. Fetal rate tracing shows a baseline heart rate of 152 / min and 2 accelerations in 10 minutes. Today's repeat ultrasound showed a permanent breech position. The patient reported that she wanted to attempt vaginal delivery. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
A. Recommend a cesarean delivery
B. Monitor up to spontaneous labor
C. Repeat the ultrasound in a week.
D. Suggest an external cephalic version
E. Suggest an internal Podalic version

A 4-year-old boy was brought to the emergency department with a fever, painful swallowing, headache, and neck spasms that began shortly after waking. He had a sore throat last week that worsened sharply this morning. He has no history of serious illness and does not take any medication. She lives at home with her mother. His older brother has asthma. His vaccinations are up-to-date. He looks seriously ill. He has a temperature of 38.4 ° C (101.2 ° F), a pulse of 95 / min, a respiratory rate of 33 / min, and a blood pressure of 93/60 mmHg. On examination, redness is observed. The neck is stiff and the extension is limited. Breathing appears labored, with the use of supporting muscles. Inspiratory striders can be heard inhaled in the auditory cavity of the chest. Cardiac examination does not show any abnormalities. Oropharyngeal examination reveals a bubble in the posterior pharyngeal wall. Venous access is established and laboratory tests are ordered. Which of the following would be the best next step in the management of this patient?
A. Endotracheal intubation
B. Antibiotics in the vein
C. Blood Cultures
D. Corticosteroids in the veins
E. CT scan of the neck
F. nebulized albuterol
G. Lateral neck X-ray

An 8-year-old boy has been brought to the doctor because he has a 7-day history of a progressive cough. Coughing occurs as spells and consists of approximately 5-10 consecutive coughs. He takes deep, noisy breaths after each spell. Sometimes he vomits after a bout of coughing. He had a runny nose for a week before he started coughing. His vaccination record is not available. He lives in an apartment with his father, mother, and two-week-old younger sister. Mom got the Tdap vaccination 11 years ago. The father's vaccination record is not available. Its temperature is 37.8 ° C (100.0 ° F). The test shows no abnormalities. His leukocyte count is 42,000 / m3. Throat swab culture and PCR results are awaited. Which of the following would be the most appropriate recommendation for this family?
A. Give oral azithromycin to the child and the father, and give the father a TDAP vaccination.
B. Give oral erythromycin to the child and the father, and give the father a TDAP vaccination.
C. Give oral azithromycin to all family members and administer the Tdap vaccination to the father and mother.
D. Give oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole to all family members and give the father a TDAP vaccination.
E. Give oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole to all family members and administer TDAP vaccination to father and mother.
F. Give oral erythromycin to all family members and administer the Tdap vaccination to the father and mother.
G. Give oral erythromycin to all family members and administer the TDAP vaccination to the father.
H. Give oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole to the father and child and give the father a TDAP vaccination.
I. Give oral azithromycin to all family members and administer the TDAP vaccination to the father.

Police brought a 23-year-old male to the emergency department for cognitive impairment and restlessness after he suffered a head injury at a local nightclub. The patient refuses to answer questions and is in a significantly unstable state. An alcoholic odor can be observed. His temperature is 36.9 ° C (98.4 ° F), pulse is 104 per minute, respiration is 24 per minute, and blood pressure is 148/95 mmHg. He is confused and only directed towards the person. Neurological tests show myosis and nystagmus but are quickly stopped after the patient tries to attack some of the care team members. A CT scan of the head shows no abnormalities. The intake of which of the following substances is likely to explain the symptoms in this patient?
A. Heroin
B. Alcohol
C. Marijuana
D. Cocaine
E. Gamma-hydroxybutyric acid
F. Lysergic acid diethylamide
G. Methamphetamine
H. Phencyclidine

A 34-year-old AIDS patient comes to the doctor because he has a two-day history of vision loss and black spots in his right eye. He does not feel any pain and has no symptoms in his left eye. He had received treatment with fluconazole for fungal esophagitis six months earlier. He was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma two years ago. Current medications include efavirenz, tenofovir, emtricitabine, azithromycin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, multivitamins, and a nutritional supplement. He is 170 cm (5 ft 7 in) tall and weighs 45 kg (99 lb); BMI is 15.6 kg / m2. It has a temperature of 37 ° C (98.6 ° F), a pulse of 89 beats per minute, and a blood pressure 110/70 mmHg. Examination reveals cervical lymphadenopathy. Numerous purple plaques can be seen on its trunk and limbs. Fundoscopic examination reveals many areas of granular yellow-white opacities and dot-blot hemorrhages around the retinal blood vessels. His CD4 + T-lymphocyte count is 36 / mm3. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Sitomegalovirus retinitis
B. Herpes simplex keratitis
C. Toxoplasma retinitis
D. HIV retinopathy
E. Varicella zoster retinitis

A 65-year-old Asian woman visits the doctor for a routine health maintenance exam. When questioned, he has experienced occasional night sweats in the last 2 months. He had no fever or weight loss. 7 months ago, he had an acute myocardial infarction and received treatment with percutaneous coronary intervention. He has hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and gastroesophageal reflux disease. He smoked a pack of cigarettes every day and has done so for 37 years. Current medications include aspirin, atorvastatin, ramipril, metoprolol, and esomeprazole. He is 178 cm (5 ft 10 in) tall and weighs 89 kg (207 lb); BMI is 29.70 kg / m2. He has a temperature of 37.4 ° C (99.3 ° F), a pulse of 84 / min, a respiratory rate of 18 / min, and a blood pressure 145/80 mmHg. The airways are clear when listening. Examination of the heart shows an S4. There is an undiagnosed skin disease near the fingernails of the right big toe. A photograph of the wound is shown. The rest of the test showed no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Cholesterol embolism
B. Traumatic subungual hemorrhage
C. Malignant melanoma
D. Onychomycosis
E. Squamous cell carcinoma

A 26-year-old African-American woman came in for a 4-day history of an aproductive cough and chest pain. The pain is sharp and increases with deep breathing. During this period, he underwent himaturia twice. Over the past six months, he has experienced periodic pain, stiffness, and swelling in his fingers and left knee. She has had two miscarriages at the ages of 22 and 24. Her only medication is minocycline for acne vulgaris. It has a temperature of 38.1 ° C (100.6 ° F), a pulse rate of 75 per minute, and a blood pressure of 138/85 mmHg. A physical examination revealed a red rash on his face. There is light sensitivity in the metacarpophalangeal joint on both sides, but no hotness or reddening. Which of the following outcomes would most likely be seen in further evaluation of this patient?
A. Anti-histone antibodies
B. Low serum levels of C3 and C4
C. during prolonged bleeding.
D. Damage to the metacarpophalangeal joint
E. Bilateral enlargement of the hilar lymph node
F. Cytotoxic glomerular antibodies

A 5-month-old male baby has been brought to the doctor by his mother because he has been suffering from a generalized itchy rash for 2-weeks. The itching often wakes the baby at night. She was strictly breastfed until she was 4 months old, after which the formula was changed to milk. His father has a history of asthma. His vaccination was complete and on time. He is in the 75th percentile in terms of length and the 70th percentile in terms of weight. Tests showed dry and peeling patches over a wide area of the face and limbs. There is no change in the inguine part. Which of the following would be the most appropriate next step in management?
A. Local Coil Tar
B. Oral acyclovir
C. Oral vitamin A
D. Local mupirocin
E. Local clotrimazole
F. Tare-enriched shampoo
G. Local emollient

After 2 hours of left femoral artery embolectomy, an obese 63-year-old woman is experiencing severe pain, numbness, and tingling in the left leg. The surgery was performed without complications and the peripheral pulses were weakly palpable after the procedure. He has type 2 diabetes, peripheral artery disease, high blood pressure, and hypercholesterolemia. Her medications before admission included insulin, enalapril, carvedilol, aspirin, and rosuvastatin. He looks uncomfortable. Her temperature is 37.1 ° C (99.3 ° F), pulse is 98 per minute, and blood pressure is 132/90 mmHg. Examination shows a cut to the left cervical spine. The left lower limb is swollen, hard, and sensitive to touch. A dorsiflexion of his left leg caused severe pain in his calf. The femoral pulse is palpable on both sides. The pedal pulse on the left side is weaker than on the right side. The laboratory results show: Hemoglobin 12. 1 Leukocyte count 11,300 / cubic millimeter Platelet count 189,000 / cubic millimeter Serum glucose 222 mg / dl Creatinine 1.1 mg / deciliter Urinalysis is within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this outcome?
A. Deep vein thrombosis
B. Reperfusion injury
C. rhabdomyolysis
D. Cholesterol embolism
E. Cellulitis

A 17-year-old boy has been brought in to the doctor for the past 3 months with progressive right knee pain. He reports that the pain is worse at night and when playing sports at school. There were no knee injuries or previous problems with his joints. His biographical indices are in the normal range. Examination of the right knee shows mild swelling and sensitivity, without heat or reddish discoloration; range of motion is limited. He walked into the Antalgic Gate. Laboratory tests showed alkaline phosphatase values of 180 units / liter and erythrocyte sedimentation rates of 80 mm / h. X-rays of the right knee are shown. Which of the following options is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Osteoclastoma
B. Ewing sarcoma
C. Cordoma
D. Osteochondroma
E. Chondrosarcoma
F. Osteosarcoma

A 17-year-old girl was brought to the doctor because she had amenorrhea for four months. Previously the seasons occurred at regular 28-day intervals and lasted 3 to 4 days. There is no family history of severe disease. He gets good grades in school and is on the high school track team. She is sexually active with a male partner and regularly uses condoms. His physique looks lean. Examination shows an enlargement of the bilateral parotid gland. The core of the body has fine fur. Serum research shows: Thyroid-stimulating hormone 3.7 μM / ml Prolactin 16 nanograms / milliliter Estradiol 23 picograms / milliliter (n > 40) Follicle-stimulating hormone 1.6 ml / ml Luteinizing hormone 2.8 ml / ml The result of a urine pregnancy test is negative. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this outcome?
A. The use of external steroids
B. Defective androgen receptor
C. Gonadal dysgenesis
D. Abnormal nerve cell migration
E. Hyperandrogenic anovulation
F. Nutritional deficiencies

A 21-year-old college student comes to the doctor with intermittent palpitations. He is not experiencing chest pain or shortness of breath. The symptoms started 2 days ago, the night she returned to her dormitory after a 4-hour-long bus ride from home. 1 day ago, he went to a party with friends. Since then, the palpitations have worsened and become more frequent. The patient smoked 5 cigarettes per day for the past 3 years. He drinks 4-6 alcoholic drinks with friends once or twice a week and occasionally uses marijuana. She is sexually active with her boyfriend and takes oral contraceptive pills. He doesn't look worried. His pulse is 100 / min and irregular, blood pressure 140/85 mmHg, and respiratory rate is 25 / min. Physical examination reveals fine tremors in both hands, hot extremities, and swollen lower legs. The sound of the breathing apparatus is clear to hear. An ECG is shown below. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
A. Measure the TSH level
B. Watch and wait
C. Give adenosine to the veins
D. Measure the D-dimer level
E. Give enoxaparin to the subcutaneous
F. send urine toxicology

A 20-year-old college student comes to the doctor because he is very sad for the last 3 weeks and has to cry constantly. 3 weeks ago, her boyfriend left her when they were together for 4 years. He has no appetite and has lost 2.3 kg (5.1 lb). She missed several classes because she couldn't stop crying or get out of bed. She always thinks about her ex-boyfriend. She said she experienced similar symptoms for about 2 months after the previous relationship ended. The patient is 158 cm (5 ft 2 in) tall and weighs 45 kg (100 lb); BMI is 18 kg / m2. Her temperature is 36.1 ° C (97 ° F), pulse is 65 per minute, and blood pressure is 110/60 mmHg. No abnormalities are seen on physical examination. He looks sad and cries easily when he checks his mental state. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Borderline personality disorder
B. grief
C. Adjustment disorder with depressive mood
D. Persistent depressive disorder
E. Major depressive disorder
F. Acute stress disorder
G. anorexia nervosa

A 16-year-old girl is brought to the doctor because her mother is concerned about her anorexia and lack of weight gain. He has lost 7 kg (15 lb) in the last 3 months. The patient says he needs to lose more weight because he doesn't want to be overweight anymore. She keeps a diary of her daily calorie intake. Menarche was 13 years old, and the last menstrual period was 3 months ago. He is on the high school track team. She is sexually active with two male partners and uses condoms infrequently. His height is in the 50th percentile and weight and BMI are below the 5th percentile. Its temperature is 37 ° C (98.6 ° F), pulse is 58 / min, and blood pressure is 96/60 mmHg. Examination reveals fine hair on the trunk and limbs. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. HIV infection
B. Body dysmorphic disorder
C. Bulimia nervosa
D. Type 1 diabetes mellitus
E. Hyperthyroidism
F. obsessive compulsive disorder
G. anorexia nervosa

A 27-year-old woman came to the emergency department because she has had increasing insensitivity and weakness in her left arm and left leg for two days. He has also experienced urinary urgency and incontinence during this period. Three months ago, he had blurred vision, difficulty distinguishing colors, and a headache for a week, all of which healed. The patient smoked a half-pack of cigarettes every day for ten years and drank four glasses of wine each week. He has a temperature of 37 ° C (98.6 ° F), a pulse of 78 per minute, a respiratory rate of 14 per minute, and a blood pressure 110/68 mmHg. Tests showed 3 / 5 strength in the left arm and leg and 5 / 5 in the right side. When the throat is flexed, the patient receives a shooting electric sensation that descends along the spine. MRIs of the brain show gadolinium-enhancing lesions in the right central sulcus, cervical spinal cord, and optic nerve. Which of the following is the best next step in the management of this patient?
A. Dimethyl fumarate therapy
B. Interferon beta therapy
C. Give Lorazepam
D. Give intravenous methylprednisolone
E. Plasmapheresis
F. Provide tissue plasminogen activator
G. Glatiramer acetate therapy

A 35-year-old male was brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after being involved in a car crash. The patient was on his way to work when he lost control of the car and hit a tree. On arrival, the patient's condition appears weak and lethargic. He has abdominal pain. He has a temperature of 37 ° C (98.6 ° F), a pulse of 121 per minute, a respiratory rate of 22 per minute, and a blood pressure 85/60 mmHg. He is aware of the individual but not of space or time. The lungs are clear when listening. Cardiac examination shows tachycardia but no murmur, rubbing, or gallop. Examination of the abdomen shows a few bruises above the umbilicus; there is extensive abdominal sensitivity. Focused assessment (FAST) is done with trauma-related sonography but the results are inconclusive. In addition to intravenous fluid resuscitation, which of the following would be the most appropriate next step in the management of this patient?
A. Angiography and embolization
B. CT scan of the abdomen
C. exploratory laparotomy
D. Entering the nasogastric tube
E. Abdominal X-ray
F. Diagnostic peritoneal lavage

A 24-year-old male with chronic back pain who visited a physician to begin care after relocating to Florida. She complained of anxiety, nausea, abdominal cramping, vomiting, and diarrhea for three days. He said not to smoke, drink alcohol, and use illegal drugs. He looks restless. It has a temperature of 37 ° C (98.6 ° F), a pulse of 110 / min, and a blood pressure of 150/86 mmHg. Physical examination shows enlarged pupillae, sweating, and hair loss. Examination of his abdomen shows extensive light sensitivity. There is no rebound tenderness or guarding. The hemoglobin concentration is 14.5 grams per deciliter, the white blood cell count is 8,000 / mm, and the platelet count is 250,000 / mm; serum studies and urinalysis show no abnormalities. Which of the following is the best pharmacotherapy?
A. Lorazepam
B. Naltrexone
C. Methadone
D. Morphine
E. Naloxone

A 38-year-old woman comes to the doctor for a follow-up visit. He has a 2-year history of depressed mood and fatigue that is consistent with morning awakening. A week ago, he started to feel less need for sleep and now feels rested after about 5 hours of sleep a night. He got two similar episodes that happened 6 months ago and 1 year ago, respectively. He reported increased energy and sexual desire. He has lost 4 kg (8.8-পাউন্ড) in the last one month. She does not feel the need for food and says that her energy comes "from the universe." She enjoyed her work as a librarian. He started taking fluoxetine 3 months ago. In mental tests, he is alert and knows the direction of time and space; he is disturbed. He has no auditory or visual hallucinations. Physical examination does not show any abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Drug-induced bilateral disorders
B. Bilateral diseases, including rapid cycling
C. delusional disorder
D. Schizoaffective disorder
E. Cyclothymic disorder
